primary.title: The Life of Saladin
primary.author: Baha ad-Din ibn Shaddad
primary.rationale: This is a contemporary biography of Saladin, written by his chief qadi and confidant. While not authored by Saladin himself, it is considered a primary source due to its direct access to information and personal accounts.

secondary.title: Saladin: The Politics of the Holy War
secondary.author: Christopher Tyerman
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive academic study of Saladin's political and military career, focusing on the context of the Crusades and the concept of 'holy war'. Tyerman is a respected historian of the Crusades.

secondary.title: The Crusades: The Authoritative History of the War for the Holy Land
secondary.author: Thomas Asbridge
secondary.rationale: While covering the broader Crusades, this book provides significant analysis of Saladin's role and impact. Asbridge is a leading scholar in the field.

secondary.title: Saladin and the Fall of Jerusalem
secondary.author: Charles Frazee
secondary.rationale: This book offers a detailed account of Saladin's life and achievements, particularly his conquest of Jerusalem. Frazee was a historian specializing in medieval history.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Saladin (letters, speeches) are scarce and often exist only within larger historical chronicles or collections, making them difficult to isolate as standalone works for digital archives. The biography by Baha ad-Din ibn Shaddad is the closest contemporary account.
